item.title: Possessing seven qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not loved, liked, respected, or emulated by his fellow celibates. What seven? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu desires gain,…
item.description:
Possessing seven qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not loved, liked, respected, or emulated by his fellow celibates. What seven? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu desires gain, desires honor, desires praise, has no moral shame, has no moral dread, has evil desires, and has wrong view. Possessing these seven qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not loved, liked, respected, or emulated by his fellow celibates.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.1

item.title: Bhikkhus, what is painful practice with slow direct knowledge? Here, a person has a very strong greedy nature, always experiencing suffering and distress born of…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, what is painful practice with slow direct knowledge? Here, a person has a very strong greedy nature, always experiencing suffering and distress born of greed; a very strong hateful nature, always experiencing suffering and distress born of hatred; a very strong deluded nature, always experiencing suffering and distress born of delusion. For that person, these five faculties appear very soft: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom. Because these five faculties are soft, he attains the immediate concentration for the destruction of the taints slowly. This, bhikkhus, is called painful practice with slow direct knowledge.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.162

item.title: Standing to one side, the devata Kassapa spoke this verse before the Blessed One: With mind liberated, The bhikkhu practices jhāna, And with the wish,…
item.description:
Standing to one side, the devata Kassapa spoke this verse before the Blessed One:

With mind liberated,
The bhikkhu practices jhāna,
And with the wish,
Attains the heart's desire.
Having known the world's
Rise and fall,
His mind pure, unattached,
He enjoys the true fruit.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.2

item.title: Elder Phussa: The seer Paṇḍara, seeing many faithful ones, Self-developed, well-guarded and restrained, Then asked the one named Phussa: 'In the future, what desires will…
item.description:
Elder Phussa:

The seer Paṇḍara, seeing many faithful ones,
Self-developed, well-guarded and restrained,
Then asked the one named Phussa:

'In the future, what desires will there be?
What aspirations? What conduct?
Please answer our question.'

'Seer Paṇḍara, listen to my words,
Receive them carefully, I will speak of the future.

'Anger and resentment,
Concealment and stubbornness,
Much deceit and envy —
Thus it will be in the future.

'Considering themselves wise,
They have gone to the far shore of the profound Dhamma,
They despise the good Dhamma,
They do not respect one another.

'Many dangers in the world
Will occur in the future.
This well-taught Dhamma,
Fools will defile.

'In the Saṅgha, those of inferior virtue
Often proclaim themselves confident and fearless.
The unlearned, the talkative, will gain a strong position.

'In the Saṅgha, those of beautiful virtue,
When they proclaim what is true, are often weak,
Shy and lacking in ardor.

'Silver, gold, fields, land,
Goats and sheep,
Male and female servants —
Fools, lacking wisdom, will accept all these in the future.

'Fools are easily angered, not calm in virtue,
Arrogant, wandering here and there,
Like beasts fond of fighting.

'They become restless, always wearing blue robes,
Deceitful and stubborn, talkative, speaking falsely,
They imitate and pretend to be like the noble ones of old.

'With oil-slicked hair, restless, eyes painted blue,
Wearing ivory-white robes, they walk on the roads.

'The well-dyed yellow robe, the banner of the Arahants,
Worn by the liberated, is not despised by them.
But they despise the yellow robe, longing to wear white.

'They become greedy for gain, lazy, of little energy,
Hard to live with in the wilderness, delighting in village life.

'Those who fear gain, always fond of wrong livelihood,
They imitate such a one, associating, not restrained.

'Those who do not gain [honor], they do not respect or honor
Those worthy of respect, the wise; they do not associate.

'Despising their own banner, delighting in external colors,
Some wear white robes, the banner of outside sects.

'Not respecting the yellow robe, in that time they are thus.
They await the yellow robe, not of a bhikkhu.

'Overcome by suffering, pierced by the dart of pain,
They await great terror.
[But] this elephant does not think about that.

'When the six-tusked elephant saw the well-dyed Arahant banner,
He uttered verses connected with the goal.

'Whoever wears the robe
With mind not free from defilements,
Not self-controlled, not truthful,
Is not worthy of the robe.

'Whoever casts off defilements,
Well established in virtue,
Self-controlled, truthful,
Is indeed worthy of the robe.

'An immoral person of inferior wisdom,
Not self-controlled, greedy,
With distracted mind, uninspired,
Is not worthy of the robe.

'One complete in virtue,
Free from greed, concentrated,
With truly pure mind,
That one is worthy of the robe.

'Whoever is arrogant and heedless,
Foolish, without virtue,
Deserves to wear white —
What need has that one of a robe?

'Bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs with defiled minds, without faith,
Will in the future oppress those with compassionate minds.

'Fools wearing robes, though taught by elders,
Of weak wisdom, will not listen, not self-controlled, greedy.

'Though taught thus, fools will not respect one another,
Will not obey the words of the teacher,
Like a wild horse [fails to obey] the charioteer.

'Thus in the future, conduct will be like that.
Bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, when the final time comes,
Be gentle and friendly, respect one another.

'Before this great calamity comes, before the great calamity arrives,
Be gentle and friendly, respect one another.

'Have a mind of loving-kindness and compassion,
Well restrained in virtue,
Devoted to energy and effort,
Always persistently inspired.

'Seeing the danger in heedlessness,
Security in non-heedlessness,
Develop the Noble Eightfold Path,
Realize the Deathless path.'

From: Theragāthā 17.1

item.title: Whatever causes — if the mind faculty were unrestrained — would give rise to craving, sorrow, and unwholesome states, that he restrains; he guards the…
item.description:
Whatever causes — if the mind faculty were unrestrained — would give rise to craving, sorrow, and unwholesome states, that he restrains; he guards the mind faculty, undertakes the restraint of the mind faculty. By means of this noble restraint of the faculties, he experiences inner well-being, without disturbance.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta

item.title: - There are these five wildernesses of the mind. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is doubtful, uncertain, not decisive, without serene confidence regarding the…
item.description:
- There are these five wildernesses of the mind. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is doubtful, uncertain, not decisive, without serene confidence regarding the Teacher. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who is doubtful, uncertain, not decisive, without serene confidence regarding the Teacher, does not incline to energy, exertion, persistence, and effort. When his mind does not incline to energy, exertion, persistence, and effort, this is called the first wilderness of the mind. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is doubtful regarding the Dhamma... regarding the Saṅgha... regarding the training... he is angry with his fellow celibates, displeased, his mind agitated, becomes wilderness. Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is angry with his fellow celibates, displeased, his mind agitated, becomes wilderness, that bhikkhu does not incline to energy, exertion, persistence, and effort. This is called the fifth wilderness of the mind. Bhikkhus, for the abandonment of these five wildernesses of the mind... the four establishments of mindfulness should be developed.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.71

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of persons existing in the world. What three? A person like a drought, a person like a local rain,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of persons existing in the world. What three? A person like a drought, a person like a local rain, and a person like rain pouring everywhere. And how, bhikkhus, is a person like a drought? Here, bhikkhus, a person does not give anything to anyone — not food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, beds, dwellings, lamps — to ascetics, brahmins, or to poor, needy, indigent beggars. Such a person, bhikkhus, is like a drought, not raining. And how, bhikkhus, is a person like a local rain? Here, bhikkhus, a person gives to some but not to others. To some ascetics, brahmins, or poor, needy, indigent beggars he gives food... lamps, but to others he does not give. Such a person, bhikkhus, is like a local rain. And how, bhikkhus, is a person like rain pouring everywhere? Here, bhikkhus, a person gives to everyone — to ascetics, brahmins, and to poor, needy, indigent beggars — food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, beds, dwellings, lamps. Bhikkhus, these are the three kinds of persons existing in the world.

From: Itivuttaka 75

item.title: Whereas some samaṇas and brahmins, while enjoying food offered by the faithful, still live maintaining themselves by wrong livelihood such as predicting: There will be…
item.description:
Whereas some samaṇas and brahmins, while enjoying food offered by the faithful, still live maintaining themselves by wrong livelihood such as predicting: There will be much rain, there will be drought, there will be a good harvest, there will be a bad harvest, there will be safety, there will be danger, there will be disease, there will be health; or they engage in occupations such as counting on fingers, accounting, adding large numbers, writing verses, worldly treatises — Samaṇa Gotama abstains from such wrong livelihood. — Bhikkhus, these are the praises of the Tathāgata by ordinary people.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 1 – Brahmajālasutta

item.title: - And, bhikkhus, when the mind is agitated, that is the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, that is the time to cultivate the…
item.description:
- And, bhikkhus, when the mind is agitated, that is the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, that is the time to cultivate the concentration enlightenment factor, that is the time to cultivate the equanimity enlightenment factor. Why is that? Because the agitated mind is easy to calm down with these things. Just as, bhikkhus, a person who wants to extinguish a great fire, if he throws wet grass, wet cow-dung, and wet wood onto it, exposes it to wind and rain, and scatters dust on it, could he extinguish that great fire?" - "Yes, Venerable Sir." - "So too, bhikkhus, when the mind is agitated, that is the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, that is the time to cultivate the concentration enlightenment factor, that is the time to cultivate the equanimity enlightenment factor. Why is that? Because the agitated mind is easy to calm down with these things. But regarding mindfulness, bhikkhus, I say that it is beneficial in every case.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 46.53

item.title: Friends, the Tathāgata is pure in bodily conduct. There is no evil bodily deed that the Tathāgata needs to hide, thinking: 'Let no one know…
item.description:
Friends, the Tathāgata is pure in bodily conduct. There is no evil bodily deed that the Tathāgata needs to hide, thinking: 'Let no one know this about me.' Friends, the Tathāgata is pure in verbal conduct. There is no evil verbal deed that the Tathāgata needs to hide, thinking: 'Let no one know this about me.' Friends, the Tathāgata is pure in mental conduct. There is no evil mental deed that the Tathāgata needs to hide, thinking: 'Let no one know this about me.'

From: Dīgha Nikāya 33 – Saṅgītisutta
